title: Michael Keane signs new one-year Everton contract
content:
Everton defender Michael Keane has signed a new one-year deal at the club.

The Athletic reported earlier this week that Everton manager David Moyes was keen to retain the 33-year-old defender, whose contract was on course to expire at the end of the season, and the club announced his new deal on Thursday.

The deal Keane signed last summer contained a club option for a further year, but Everton have instead offered him a new contract on fresh terms, rewarding his improved performances this season.

The former Manchester United and Burnley man is considered an important part of the defensive unit and has filled in well at centre-back in the absence of the injury-hit Jarrad Branthwaite.

“We’re pleased to have extended Michael’s long service at Everton,“ Moyes said. ”He is an experienced and respected member of the squad, who knows the standards we expect at the club.

“Michael has been consistent all season and he’ll continue to be a valuable part of our squad going into next season.”

A 2017 signing from Burnley, Keane will head into his tenth season with Everton. He has made 30 appearances this campaign across all competitions, scoring three times and helping Moyes’ side to 11 clean sheets — the fourth-best defensive record in the Premier League.

“The club means a lot,” Keane said. “It’s one of those things that’s easy to say, but it has become part of me. It’s who I am and it feels like family to me — the people around the club, the fans, the players, the staff. So it’s really special to me and I couldn’t really imagine my life without Everton.

“I think it’s been a great season for me personally. I’ve played a lot of football — probably more than I expected – and I feel like I’ve done well and I’ve absolutely loved it. So to get my 10th year here, I think it’s a big achievement and one I’m proud of.

“Ten years is a long time. I’ve seen a lot here and been through a lot and it’s good now we’re in a much better place than what we have been in the past. I go into my 10th season looking really positive, and thinking what we can achieve and where we can be is really exciting.”

Keane’s extension brings Everton some certainty in defence at a time when they are counting the cost of Branthwaite’s latest setback. The 33-year-old has been an able deputy for his younger team-mate throughout the season, impressing Moyes with his work ethic and performance levels. There is a sense the defender has benefitted from extra game time and being able to develop a rhythm.

Keane is viewed as a solid presence around the dressing room and that was a key reason why he was retained last summer, during a period of churn for the squad. Moyes wanted to keep a core of players who were reliable and could help drive standards, with the central defender seen as one such figure.

This latest deal, nearly a year on, is best seen as a reward for his work so far this campaign. Critically, this is a new contract, with the decision taken early in talks not to merely activate the club’s one-year extension option. The push was for fresh terms to highlight his progress and increased role.

Keane’s deal gives Moyes a reliable fourth central defensive option for next season — the plan is to sign a new right-back and move Jake O’Brien back inside into his favoured position. It gives them able cover to compensate for Branthwaite’s absence, should his injury problems persist, and allows them to focus more resources on weaker parts of the squad, including full-back.
